$comment: docs/e2ee/WIRE.md §14.1's shared fixture table: `handle.rs::eligibility`/`not_signed_in` (Rust, the shipped backend) and `mock.ts::evaluateHandle` (the TypeScript mock) are each asserted against this exact table so a future edit that drifts either one from the other, or from this table, fails a test rather than shipping unnoticed (#838, refs #820). `input: null` exercises `not_signed_in()`/the no-signed-in-account branch; every other `input` exercises `eligibility(input)`/the string branch of `evaluateHandle`. `reason` values are `IneligibilityReason`'s kebab-case wire form (models.rs `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]`, types.ts `IneligibilityReasonSchema`).

cases.label: empty_username_is_punctuation_not_not_signed_in
cases.$comment: WIRE.md §14.1: '{1,30}' has no length floor of its own, so the reference implementation states the empty case explicitly rather than relying on the regex — and mock.ts's own #838 regression, folding this case into the null case, is exactly the drift this fixture exists to catch.

cases.label: non_ascii_cyrillic_homograph
cases.$comment: U+0430 CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER A prefixing 'lice' — the homograph §11.3 exists to keep out of the charset entirely.

cases.label: kelvin_sign_is_non_ascii_not_folded_to_k
cases.$comment: WIRE.md §14.1 step 1: U+212A KELVIN SIGN must be rejected as non-ascii on the raw string. `"\u212A".toLowerCase()` is `"k"` under Unicode case folding, so a fold-first (or ascii_lower-via-String.toLowerCase-before-the-ASCII-check) implementation would wrongly accept this as a plain ASCII handle.
